bullets.title: INTC: Q3 EPS beats but Q4/2027 PC outlook catastrophic; 4 firms cut ratings
bullets.body: Intel Q3 revenue $16.5B and EPS $0.52 beat consensus, but Q4 guided $15-16B (vs. $17B Street), sending the stock down ~25% on the day—worst session since 1974. PC unit market expected down ~12% CY26 with ~10% further decline in 2027 as memory price shocks destroy demand; 2027 is guided as a negative-FCF investment year. Data Center/AI revenue grew +77.8% YoY and foundry improved, but cannot offset client collapse. BofA and Roth Capital downgraded to Neutral; multiple PTs slashed (BofA $100, Roth $70, Citi keeps Buy at $100, MS cuts to $75). Additional Israel Fab 28 explosion adds ~$300M quarterly revenue drag in Q4/Q1.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS guides 40%+ growth in 2027-28, but Q3 missed elevated buy-side bar
bullets.body: AWS grew 39.3% YoY to $46B in Q3, beating consensus but missing the ~42-43% buy-side bogey. Management guided AWS growth above 40% for both 2027 and 2028—the first time Amazon has given specific future-year guidance—with a $578B backlog up $82B QoQ. North America retail margin expanded ~320bps to 7.7% YoY. Q3 capex $77.3B was 31.7% above consensus; FY26 ~$220B with 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Stock fell ~7% pre-market on FCF concerns and Q4 operating income guide of $28.5-33.5B (midpoint ~$1.5B below Street). Hedgeye upgraded to top long citing 30% upside over 12-15 months; JPM raises 2027 capex estimate to $395B.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure 48% growth beats, FQ2 guide 49-50%; $25B bond deal, 60K voluntary buyouts
bullets.body: Microsoft beat F1Q27 on all key metrics—revenue $92.3B (+19% YoY), EPS $4.89 (+27%), Azure +48% cc vs. 44-45% consensus, operating margin ~50%. F2Q Azure guided 49-50%, indicating acceleration; Copilot daily users +50% QoQ. MSFT also issued $25B in investment-grade bonds (first since 2017) and offered voluntary buyouts to ~60,000 employees (~27% of headcount). Goldman raises MSFT PT; Piper raises to $650 OW. FCF remains positive despite AI capex build, making MSFT the preferred 'quality AI' play vs. negative-FCF hyperscalers.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Search misses badly (-12% vs. +14-15% expected); stock -12.6% worst single-day on record
bullets.body: Alphabet Q3 Search & Other grew only 12% YoY (vs. 14-15% expected), with AI Mode queries monetizing at lower rates than traditional search. YouTube also missed. Google Cloud grew 103% YoY—a strong beat—but $51.4B quarterly capex driving negative FCF. FY26 capex guidance maintained at $195-205B with 'significant' 2027 increase flagged. Hedgeye and Citi (PT cut to $375) maintain buys; DA Davidson Neutral at $300 on margin pressure and capex concerns. JPM Tech Sketch notes GOOGL TPUs now available on Oracle OCI and OpenAI signed up as TPU buyer.

bullets.title: NOW: Q3 beats but Q4 cRPO guide 18.5% (vs. 20%+ expected) sends stock -18-27%
bullets.body: ServiceNow Q3 subscription revenue and EPS were modest beats, but Q4 cRPO guidance of 18.5% constant currency decelerated sharply from 21% in Q3 and came 150bps below consensus. AI ACV target raised to $1.7B (+70% YTD) but markets question whether AI deployments are dilutive to near-term subscription growth. Non-GAAP subscription gross margin fell 300bps YoY for fourth consecutive quarter on AI inference and public cloud costs. Armis acquisition and FDE accounting shifts contributed ~175bps to Q4 cRPO. Wolfe maintains Peer Perform; Citi and JPM both cut PTs.

bullets.title: RDDT: DAU miss and Google search-referral cliff send stock -36% on the week
bullets.body: Reddit Q3 ad revenue grew 54% YoY on strong CPMs, but U.S. DAUs declined ~2.5M QoQ and Google AI Mode is removing ~1M search referrals per week, risking low-double-digit Q4 DAU decline. Company is pivoting to a fully logged-in platform (logged-in users ~80% of monetization, 5x more engaged). Citi cuts PT to $186 but maintains Buy; Raymond James cuts to $150 Strong Buy; Opco downgrades to Perform. Piper cuts PT to $145.

bullets.title: SNDK: Massive Q3 beat/raise; AI storage demand locked through end of decade
bullets.body: SanDisk (formerly WDC spin) reported September quarter revenue $11.03B (+23% QoQ, beat), EPS $49.51 (beat guidance by ~$5), gross margin 85.1%. December guidance $12.2-12.6B with GM 84.5-85.5%, ~10 points above Street. ~50% of FY27 bits and ~67% of FY28 bits already under long-term agreements; NBM pipeline exceeds available supply through 2030. Announced 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov 19. Citi maintains Buy at $2,100 PT; Mizuho reiterates Outperform at $1,900 PT.

bullets.title: DASH acquires CART for ~$17B; JPM suspends both ratings on advisory conflict
bullets.body: DoorDash announced acquisition of Instacart at ~$65/share (~$17B equity value, ~26% premium) in a deal expected to close end-2027/1H2028. 3Q DASH core orders +17% YoY, U.S. restaurant GOV fastest growth in five years, DashPass at ATH. CART FY27 EBITDA deal synergy potential $500M+ (net of investments, reinvested Year 1). Citi reiterates Buy on DASH ($255 PT, ~50% upside); JPM suspended ratings on both citing advisory conflict.

bullets.title: MRVL in advanced talks to acquire LITE in all-stock deal at modest premium
bullets.body: Bloomberg/CNBC reported Marvell Technology in advanced discussions to acquire Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock deal at 'not a large premium'; announcement could come as early as next week. LITE +7-10% on reports; MRVL -6-11%. Strategic rationale: vertical integration of optical DSPs with lasers/photonics for AI CPO interconnect. Wolfe sees logic but questions timing at peak valuations (LITE ~30x LTM rev); notes NVDA equity investment in LITE complicates deal. Citi maintains Buy on LITE at $1,400 PT; Morgan Stanley sees MRVL deal as risky at cycle peak.

bullets.title: AMD: Q3 consensus $13.1B rev, $1.95 EPS; Data Center expected $8.25B; options imply ~9%
bullets.body: AMD reports Q3 earnings (Nov 3) with consensus at $13.09B revenue and $1.95 EPS. Data Center segment expected $8.25B (71% of implied Q4 at $11.6B). C27 AI GPU revenue modeled at $42B with upside to $48B on 14K racks, but supply constraints may limit execution. Street checks suggest this will be a solid print with no negative INTC read-through for server business. Options imply ~8.9% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: ORCL Investor Day: FCF positive H2'28, $30B+ FY29, $225B+ FY30 revenue; stock +10%
bullets.body: Oracle's October 28 AI World/Investor Day impressed investors: company targets $225B+ revenue by FY30 (35% CAGR), will raise only ~$20B incremental capital through FY30, and expects FCF positive in H2 FY28 with $30B+ in FY29 vs. prior consensus of FCF burn. Plans 10GW capacity by FY28 at ~$37B/GW build cost. Vendor financing, customer prepayments, and bring-your-own-hardware reduce upfront needs ~50%. 80% buy-rated; avg PT $240.84 (66% upside from ~$145).

bullets.title: META: $95B equity raise ($35B secondary + $60B ATM); NVDA, AMD, AVGO invest $5B
bullets.body: Meta priced a $22.5B forward share sale + $12.5B mandatory convertible preferred ($35B combined) with NVDA/AMD/AVGO as $5B aggregate anchor investors, and registered a $60B Class C ATM to commence Q1 2027. FY27 capex guided $135-145B (after narrowing FY26 to same range). 2027 capex consensus implies +59% from Q3 run rate. Q3 EPS beat consensus by 3.8% vs. -6.9% expected. Stock fell ~15% on the month on capex/dilution concerns before partial recovery. Hedgeye maintains long on core advertising strength; 22V neutral into year-end.

bullets.title: RBLX: Q3 bookings beat but Q4 AEBITDA guide -$70M to -$10M well below $414M consensus
bullets.body: Roblox Q3 bookings $1.70B beat consensus $1.63B, but Q4 bookings guided $1.89-2.00B (midpoint roughly in line) while Q4 covenant Adj. EBITDA guided $320-380M vs. $414M Street—a 12% miss at mid-point driven by AI infrastructure spend. GTA VI launch risk (Nov 19) and age verification headwinds weighed on sentiment. Citi cuts PT to $55 (from $60) but maintains Buy; DA Davidson neutral at $54 PT.

bullets.title: PINS: Q3 revenue miss, Q4 guide below consensus; EU headwinds and Google referral risk
bullets.body: Pinterest Q3 missed revenue consensus modestly on EU de-minimis/tariff headwinds and Google search referral pressures (European ARPU -8%). 12th consecutive quarter of low-double-digit MAU growth but monetization lagging. Q4 guidance below Street. DA Davidson cuts PT to $70 (from prior higher level), maintains Neutral; Piper cuts PT to $145 (from $195) with Buy; OPCO cuts PT to $25 from $30. Expected acceleration in 2027 as EU challenges ease and GTM restructuring pays off.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY OSB GGR up 36% MTD on hold expansion; UBS maintains Buy at $48 PT
bullets.body: DraftKings NY October MTD GGR +36% YoY with hold rate up +240bps to 9.3%, despite handle growth flat YoY. Week-of-10/25 GGR +67% YoY on 11.6% hold (+510bps). Market share stable at 32-32.5% GGR. Missouri first full month showed DKNG at 40% handle share ($129M). UBS maintains Buy at $48 PT based on 17x 2028E EV/EBITDA.

bullets.title: HOOD: Q3 EPS miss on lower crypto revenues; $6.3B Binance hack adds sentiment pressure
bullets.body: Robinhood Q3 EPS $0.51 missed consensus $0.56 on lower take rates and crypto market weakness; stock -13.5% on the week. The $6.3B Binance security breach (largest crypto exchange hack on record) added negative sentiment for crypto-adjacent fintech names. Morgan Stanley cut estimates/valuation on COIN and GEMI; HOOD cited as having less direct earnings risk but near-term sentiment headwind. FY26 adjusted operating expense guidance narrowed to $2.675-2.75B.

bullets.title: AFRM: BNPL TAM analysis bullish; expected to capture 40-45% of incremental U.S. growth
bullets.body: UBS estimates U.S. BNPL eCommerce 'True TAM' at ~$2.8T in 2026E with only 4.6% penetrated; BNPL volume expected to grow ~21% CAGR 2026-2030. Affirm positioned to capture ~40-45% of incremental growth via data advantage, merchant-funded 0% APR loans, and Amazon/Shopify partnerships. Affirm also announced partnerships with Intuit (~$2T GMV) and ServiceTitan. AFRM +1.8% on lower interest rates in the week.

bullets.title: RCL: Q3 beat/raise; 2027 bookings up high-teens at record rates; $20-handle EPS target intact
bullets.body: Royal Caribbean Q3 adjusted EPS $6.57 beat $6.26-$6.36 guidance on close-in Europe/Caribbean strength; FY26 EPS guidance raised to $17.85-$17.95. 2027 bookings pacing high-teens ahead of historical levels at record rates; customer deposits up ~8% QoQ. Citi raises PT to $364; JPM raises FY27 EPS to $20.49, OW $394 PT; Mizuho raises to $380. '$20 handle' EPS target for 2027 firmly intact.

bullets.title: VRT: Q3 beat 15% above consensus; organic orders +100%; raises FY26/FY27 guidance
bullets.body: Vertiv Q3 revenue $4.31B was ~15% above Street consensus on Americas organic acceleration to 66% growth; organic orders +100% YoY. FY26 revenue raised to $14.45-14.85B; FY27 revenue target raised to $19.6B with EPS $10.10. GEV also reported strong beat: orders +96% organically, raised guidance, increased buyback from $10B to $20B, and announced $9B Trench Group acquisition at 13x '28 EV/EBITDA. ROTH raises VRT PT to $345.

bullets.title: GLW: Optical revenue +44% YoY; Q4 guide above consensus; Springboard plan accelerating
bullets.body: Corning Q3 core EPS $0.91 beat $0.88 consensus; optical communications revenue $2.38B grew +44% YoY (+84% enterprise optical). Q4 guided EPS $0.96-1.00 (vs. $0.93 consensus) and revenue $5.2-5.3B. Free cash flow $661M significantly exceeded $274M estimate. Citi maintains Buy at $220 PT; JPM neutral but acknowledges optical beat; Wolfe hosts callback webcast.
